content.description: base64 bytes on write; the server hashes + stores them (never returned)

from.description:
From is the RFC3339 start of the metric window. Empty means all time, treated as a
single reporting period (see monthsBetween).

question.description:
Question is the plain-language question about the org's books, e.g. "what is my
MRR?". Longer than 2000 characters is truncated, never refused.

to.description: To is the RFC3339 end of the metric window. Empty means up to now.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt and UpdatedAt are unix seconds, both server-assigned.

event.description:
Event is the analytics event a member must have fired. EMPTY MEANS NO
FILTER: the audience is then every mailable customer in the org, and no
warehouse is consulted.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned audience id ("aud_" + 128 random bits).

name.description: Name is the audience's label. Required, trimmed, capped at 1024 bytes.

windowDays.description:
WindowDays is how far back the event counts, ending now. 0 means 30 and
nothing above 3650 is honoured. Ignored when Event is empty.

url.description: URL is the upstream server, http(s)://host[:port].

weight.description: Weight is this member's share of the round-robin; must be >= 0.

org.description:
Org is the tenant to migrate. Required — there is no fleet-wide form of this
cutover, because each org must be reconciled on its own.

override.description:
Override books this bill even when one of the SAME economic identity
(vendor, total, issue date) already posted — the explicit human confirmation that a
same-looking bill is a genuine second spend, not the same receipt re-scanned.

scanId.description:
ScanID is the scanned document's file hash, as GET /v1/books/inbox and the scan
draft report it. It is the idempotency key: re-booking the same scan writes nothing.

voucher.description:
Voucher is the reviewed voucher to post. Its source is FORCED to (scan, scanId)
server-side, so it can never be booked under another source's key.

body.description: Body is the post text. Required.

channel.description:
Channel is the target network: x, facebook, instagram, linkedin, tiktok,
youtube or threads. Required — a post must name where it goes.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt and UpdatedAt are unix seconds, both server-assigned.

error.description:
Error is the exact reason the last publish attempt failed — the honest
record behind a "failed" status, never a faked success.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned post id ("cal_" + 128 random bits).

publishedAt.description: PublishedAt is when the publish succeeded; 0 until it does.

scheduledAt.description:
ScheduledAt is the unix publish time; 0 leaves the post a draft, and any
value makes it "scheduled" for the durable sweep to pick up.

status.description: Status is draft, scheduled, published, failed or canceled. Server-owned.

title.description: Title is the post's internal label, capped at 1024 bytes.

budget.description: Budget and Spend are minor units (USD cents), clamped to >= 0.

channel.description:
Channel is the delivery surface: email, sms, social, meta, google or
tiktok. Empty means email.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt and UpdatedAt are unix seconds, both server-assigned.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned campaign id ("camp_" + 128 random bits).

name.description: Name is the campaign's label. Required, trimmed, capped at 1024 bytes.

objective.description: Objective is the free-text goal ("signups"), capped at 1024 bytes.

scheduledAt.description:
ScheduledAt is the unix send time; 0 means unscheduled. Setting it on a
campaign with no explicit status makes that status "scheduled".

status.description:
Status is the lifecycle: draft, scheduled, active, paused or completed.
Empty means draft.

max_age.description: MaxAge caps message age, e.g. "24h" or "7d"; "0" (default) is unlimited.

max_bytes.description: MaxBytes caps the stream's total stored bytes; -1 (default) is unlimited.

max_msg_size.description: MaxMsgSize caps one message's size in bytes; -1 (default) is the broker's limit.

max_msgs.description: MaxMsgs caps the number of stored messages; -1 (default) is unlimited.

name.description: Name is the stream name, unique within the org (alphanumeric, hyphens, underscores).

num_replicas.description: Replicas is the number of stream replicas (1–5); this plane runs 1.

retention.description: Retention is the retention policy: limits (default), interest, or workqueue.

storage.description: Storage is the storage backend: file (default) or memory.

subjects.description: Subjects are the org-relative subjects bound to this stream (wildcards supported). Default: the stream name.

cordon.description: Cordon true marks the node unschedulable; false restores it.

drain.description: Drain additionally evicts the pods already running there.

id.description: ID is the node's droplet id, from the path.

disk.description:
Disk requests a PERMANENT resize that grows the disk. DO can never resize such a
droplet down again, so it defaults false — a CPU/RAM-only change, reversible.

id.description: ID is the DO droplet id, from the path. Numeric.

size.description: Size is the target DigitalOcean size slug on resize, e.g. "s-4vcpu-8gb".

address.description:
Address is a single recipient, normalized (lower-cased, trimmed) before
use. Give this OR audienceId, never both and never neither.

audienceId.description:
AudienceID fans the sequence out over a saved audience, resolved live to
the org's mailable customers. Email only.

channel.description:
Channel is the delivery surface; empty means email. An audience resolves
mailboxes, so an audience enroll must be email.

id.description: ID is the sequence id from the path.

keywords.description:
Keywords keeps only items whose TITLE contains one of these,
case-insensitively. They are also the GDELT queries the feed fans out to,
one per keyword of three characters or more — so a keyword both widens what
is fetched and narrows what is kept.

regions.description:
Regions keeps only items whose TITLE contains one of these, matched
case-insensitively as a substring. Empty keeps every region.

sources.description:
Sources keeps only items whose outlet name contains one of these,
case-insensitively. Empty keeps every outlet.

decidedBy.description:
DecidedBy is who settled a terminal KYC status: the provider name, or a
reviewer's user id.

email.description:
Email is the founder's email, and the key a KYC decision addresses a founder
by — POST /v1/company/kyc/decision matches on it.

equityBps.description:
EquityBps is the founder's ownership in basis points, 0–10000 (1% == 100 bps,
so 10000 is the whole company). The founders' shares seed the cap-table genesis.

kycRef.description: KYCRef is the idv provider's session reference for this founder.

kycStatus.description:
KYCStatus is the founder's identity-verification state: pending, verified (a
real idv provider reported a pass), reviewer_confirmed (a privileged reviewer
confirmed out-of-band) or failed. The payment stage is unreachable until every
founder passes.

name.description: Name is the founder's full legal name, as it appears on the formation documents.

amountCents.description:
AmountCents is the credit, in whole cents. Must be positive and within the
per-grant cap.

currency.description: Currency is the ISO code, lower-cased. Empty means usd.

org.description: Org is the tenant to credit. Required.

reason.description: Reason is the operator's justification, recorded on the audit row.

source.description:
Source is the money bucket: "trial" (default) for a non-cash comp that is never
refundable, or "prepaid" for real money. Anything unknown falls back to trial.

user.description:
User optionally names a MEMBER to credit, by bare IAM username. Empty credits
the org. Which of the two the money actually lands on is decided by
account.Payer, not here: a pooled org keeps one balance whatever is named.

id.description: an experiment (run) stable id

account.description: Account is the chart-of-accounts number this side posts to, e.g. "5300".

credit.description: Credit is the leg's credit in exact cents. Set this or Debit, not both.

debit.description: Debit is the leg's debit in exact cents. Set this or Credit, not both.

config.description:
Config is the transform's parameters: redirectScheme takes scheme (default
https) and permanent ("true" ⇒ 301, else 302); stripPrefix REQUIRES
prefixes (comma-separated, first match wins); addPrefix REQUIRES prefix;
headers is a header→value map set on the response.

id.description:
ID identifies the transform within the org: [A-Za-z0-9-_.], at most 128
chars. A create that omits it gets a generated one. Routes reference it by
this id.

type.description: Type is the transform: redirectScheme, stripPrefix, addPrefix or headers.

name.description: Name is the app, from the path.

scope.description: Scope "host" applies here only; default "fleet" applies everywhere.

cache_paths.description:
CachePaths overrides CacheTTLSec per path PREFIX (key "/v1/models" → seconds).
The longest matching prefix wins.

cache_ttl_sec.description:
CacheTTLSec is the org's default edge-cache TTL for its responses, in seconds;
0 means no caching. Unset inherits the platform default.

cors_origins.description:
CORSOrigins is the PLATFORM-scope CORS allowlist EdgeCORS admits: an exact
origin, a bare host, or a "*.host" wildcard. Writable only by a SuperAdmin —
CORS is evaluated before identity, so it has no tenant to scope to.

methods.description:
Methods is the allowlist of HTTP methods the edge accepts for this org. Empty
means all are accepted.

org_rpm.description:
OrgRPM is the org's OWN authenticated rate ceiling, requests per minute, as
ScopeRateLimit enforces it. Unset inherits the platform default, then the
static boot default.

per_ip_rpm.description:
PerIPRPM is the PLATFORM-scope pre-auth flood cap: requests EdgeRateLimit
admits per WindowSec from one client IP. SuperAdmin-only, same reason.

updated_at.description:
UpdatedAt is the unix second this policy row was last written. Server-stamped;
a client-supplied value is ignored.

updated_by.description:
UpdatedBy is the validated user id that wrote this policy row. Server-stamped;
a client-supplied value is ignored.

window_sec.description: WindowSec is the window PerIPRPM is counted over, in seconds. SuperAdmin-only.

filter.description: Filter purges only messages on this org-relative subject (wildcards supported).

keep.description: Keep retains that many newest messages.

name.description: Name is the stream name, from the path.

code.description: Code is the promo code from the path.

instrument.description:
Instrument identifies the payment method. It is the anti-farming key: one
redemption per instrument, fleet-wide.

plan.description: Plan is the plan being redeemed against: pro, max or team.

seats.description:
Seats is the Team seat count; 0 means 1. Seats beyond the promo's
teamSeatCap bill at list.

name.description: Name is the app, from the path. It must be one the manifest declares.

scope.description:
Scope "host" applies here only. Default "fleet" rolls it out one host at
a time, halting on the first host that fails to come up.

url.description:
URL is the artifact directly, for an origin with no index. Sum is its hex
SHA-256 and is REQUIRED with it: zip refuses an unverified download, and
so does this.

version.description:
Version is a release tag, resolved to a URL and digest through the
origin's binaries.json index — the same index CI publishes, so there is
no second table mapping versions to digests.

glossary.description:
Glossary is the terminology the entry was translated under. Its VERSION — the
digest of the sorted terms — is part of the entry's identity, so editing a term
yields a new entry rather than overwriting the old rendering.

source.description:
Source is the ORIGINAL string this entry translates. Required; part of the
entry's identity, so a different source is a different entry.

state.description:
State is the entry's new position on the review ladder: suggested, approved or
published. `machine` is engine-only and is refused here — a human may not demote
a string back into the churn.

target.description:
Target is the target language tag (BCP-47, e.g. "es" or "pt-BR"). Required;
part of the entry's identity.

text.description:
Text is the reviewed translation to store. A human write always wins over the
stored value.

tier.description:
Tier is the engine tier the entry belongs to, quality (the default) or bulk.
Part of the entry's identity: the two tiers keep separate renderings.

name.description: Name is the round's name on the cap table, e.g. "Seed". Required.

preMoneyValuation.description: PreMoneyValuation is the valuation the round prices off, before the new money.

pricePerShare.description: PricePerShare is the per-share price of a priced round.

roundType.description: RoundType is PRICED, SAFE or CONVERTIBLE_NOTE. Defaults to PRICED.

shareClassId.description: ShareClassID is the cap table's share class the round issues into.

targetAmount.description:
TargetAmount is the amount the round is raising, recorded verbatim on the
canonical cap table's rounds.create contract.

host.description:
Host is the exact hostname this route matches, lowercased with any trailing
dot stripped. It is a GLOBALLY unique claim — one route across the whole
edge may hold a host, so no tenant can hijack another's.

id.description:
ID identifies the route within the org: [A-Za-z0-9-_.], at most 128 chars.
A create that omits it gets a generated one.

middlewares.description:
Middlewares are the ids of the edge transforms to apply, in this order,
before the request reaches the service. At most 16.

pathPrefix.description:
PathPrefix narrows the match to requests under this path; it must start
with "/". Empty matches every path on the host.

priority.description:
Priority orders routes that share a host: higher wins, and equal priorities
fall back to the longer PathPrefix.

service.description:
Service is the id of the backend pool this route dispatches to. A route
naming a service that does not exist is skipped at compile, not served.

tls.description: TLS asks the edge to terminate TLS for Host with an ACME-managed certificate.

category.description:
Category is the COA expense account a matching bill books to. An upsert normalizes
a slug ("cloud") to its account number.

pattern.description:
Pattern is the merchant substring the rule matches on, case-insensitively. It is
also the key an upsert writes by.

priority.description: Priority breaks ties: when several patterns match, the highest wins.

document.description:
Document is the raw CycloneDX bill of materials, any JSON. Its components[]
are flattened and persisted; nothing else is read or stored.

format.description: Format names the document format; "cyclonedx" is the only one parsed.

gitSha.description: GitSha is the commit the image was built from.

imageDigest.description:
ImageDigest is the content-addressed digest (sha256:…) the components are
keyed under. Required — it, not a tenant, is what an SBOM belongs to.

imageRef.description:
ImageRef is the human-readable image reference the digest was published as.
A resolve matches on either this or the digest.

sourceRepo.description: SourceRepo is the repository the image was built from.

count.description: Count is the node count to set.

id.description: ID is the DOKS cluster id, from the path.

pool.description:
Pool is the node pool, from the path. Its DO id or its name — both are unique
within a cluster, and an operator reads the name off the board.

id.description: ID is the campaign id from the path.

scheduledAt.description: ScheduledAt is the unix send time. 0 clears the schedule.

createdAt.description: CreatedAt and UpdatedAt are unix seconds, both server-assigned.

id.description: ID is the server-assigned sequence id ("seq_" + 128 random bits).

name.description: Name is the sequence's label. Required, trimmed, capped at 1024 bytes.

status.description:
Status is the lifecycle: draft, active or archived. Empty means draft, and
ONLY an active sequence accepts enrollments.

id.description: ID is the sequence id from the path.

status.description:
Status is draft, active or archived. Required; there is no default here,
unlike on create. Only an active sequence accepts enrollments.

backends.description: Backends are the upstream servers to balance across: 1..32 of them.

id.description:
ID identifies the pool within the org: [A-Za-z0-9-_.], at most 128 chars.
A create that omits it gets a generated one. Routes reference it by this id.

passHostHeader.description:
PassHostHeader forwards the client's original Host header upstream instead
of rewriting it to the backend's.

email.description: Email is the address the signature request is sent to.

name.description: Name is the recipient's name, as it appears on the signature request.

body.description: Body is the message text. Required.

delaySeconds.description:
DelaySeconds is how long after the previous step this one sends (after
enrollment, for the first step). Must be >= 0.

id.description: SequenceID is the sequence id from the path (the route's :id).

subject.description: Subject is the email subject line, capped at 1024 bytes.

address.description:
Address is the recipient, normalized (lower-cased, trimmed) so an opt-out
cannot be slipped past on a case or whitespace difference. Required.

channel.description:
Channel is the surface opted out of: email, sms, social, meta, google or
tiktok. Empty means email. Opting out of one leaves the others reachable.

reason.description:
Reason is a free-text note, capped at 1024 bytes. The public one-click
endpoint records "one-click unsubscribe".

acmeEmail.description:
ACMEEmail is the ACME account email. It binds an account for the lifetime
of an edge process, so it applies only when the edge (re)starts.

extraHosts.description:
ExtraHosts get certificates without owning a route — at most 256. They feed
the ACME HostPolicy and hot-apply on the next reload.

staging.description:
Staging issues from Let's Encrypt's staging directory (untrusted certs, high
rate limits). Like ACMEEmail it applies only when the edge (re)starts.

framework.description: only when it differs from the template's

id.description: selector, unique within the template ("react", "grid-3-fluid")

kind.description: the axis it varies: format | page | theme

source.description: the repository this shape is forked from; the synthesized default shape carries the template's own

aliases.description:
Aliases are the other spellings a receipt may print the vendor under; a scan
matching any of them resolves to this vendor.

canonical.description: Canonical is the vendor's one true name, and the key an upsert writes by.

defaultCategory.description:
DefaultCategory is the COA expense account new bills from this vendor book to.
An upsert normalizes a slug ("software") to its account number.

id.description: ID is the DO volume id, from the path.

name.description:
Name is the snapshot name on the snapshot action. Blank gets a deterministic
"<volume>-predelete-<unix>" so the undo is findable in the DO console.

sizeGiB.description:
SizeGiB is the target size on the resize action. A volume only ever grows —
ExpandTo is the verdict that refuses a shrink, so this is not validated here.

snapshot.description:
Snapshot is the snapshot-first switch on DELETE. Anything other than the literal
"false" snapshots before destroying — the snapshot IS the undo, so waiving it is
deliberate and explicit.

description.description: Description is the human line for the event, e.g. the vendor a bill came from.

legs.description:
Legs are the sides of the posting. They must balance: Σdebit == Σcredit, give or
take the 2¢ round-off allowance.

postingAt.description:
PostingAt is the RFC3339 instant the event posts at — the time every statement
window filters on.

sourceId.description:
SourceID is the source event's own id within that namespace. Together with
SourceKind it is the key that makes a repeat posting a no-op.

sourceKind.description: SourceKind is the idempotency namespace naming what booked this, e.g. "scan".

id.description: ID is the accreditation record to decide, from the path.

status.description:
Status is the decision being recorded: reviewer_confirmed, provider_verified,
rejected, or expired.

basis.description:
Basis is the qualification category: income, net_worth, professional_license,
or entity.

evidenceDocId.description: EvidenceDocID references an evidence document in the org's sealed data room.

expiresAt.description: ExpiresAt is the unix second a confirmation ages out; 0 means none.

method.description:
Method is how the state was established: self_attested, third_party_letter,
or provider_verified.

note.description: Note is a non-PII operator note.

status.description:
Status may only be "asserted" (empty reads as asserted); every confirmed,
rejected or expired state is recorded via the decision endpoint.

subjectId.description: SubjectID names the subject this record is about; it must exist within the org.

activate.description: Activate switches these tool names on for the caller's org and project.

deactivate.description: Deactivate switches these tool names off.

id.description: ID is the annotation queue to add to, from the path.

items.description:
Items are the objects to enqueue for review, 1–200 per request. Each names
exactly one object.

code.description: Explicit code override. If omitted, the requested vanity code or a derived slug is used.

amountCents.description: Payout amount in USD cents (must be positive; cannot exceed pending commission).

method.description: Payout method. `credits` issues a commerce grant; any other value (wire/paypal/check/…) is record-only.

reference.description: Optional external reference for a cash payout.

to.description:
To is the target stage: structure, founders, payment, documents, esign,
genesis, import or company.

requestedCode.description: Optional requested vanity code (3–32 chars of a–z, 0–9, hyphen). Staff approves and mints it.

code.description: The affiliate code the referred org arrived with (from an `?aff=` link).

message.description: Optional steering text (max 16 KiB). Required for the message command when no payload is given.

payload.description: Optional arbitrary JSON payload (max 64 KiB); must be valid JSON.
Arbitrary JSON payload (max 64 KiB); must be valid JSON.

input.description: Caller input appended to the agent's instructions (capped at 128 KiB).

accessGroups.description:
AccessGroups REPLACES the org's named access groups, as
group name -> channel -> entries. Absent or null leaves them alone.

channel.description:
Channel is the transport to edit: discord, slack, teams or telegram.
Required; an unknown value is a 404.

dm.description:
DM REPLACES the config-managed DM allow entries. Absent or null leaves them
alone; an empty list clears them. It never touches senders approved through
pairing — a policy edit cannot revoke an approved pairing.

dmPolicy.description:
DMPolicy sets how direct messages are admitted: "pairing" (a person must be
approved first), "allowlist" (only listed senders) or "open". Empty leaves
it unchanged.

group.description:
Group REPLACES the config-managed group allow entries. Absent or null
leaves them alone; an empty list clears them.

groupPolicy.description:
GroupPolicy sets how group and thread rooms are admitted: "open",
"allowlist" or "disabled". Empty leaves it unchanged.

channel.description: Channel is the transport the request came in on: discord, slack, teams or telegram.

code.description:
Code is the pairing code from GET /v1/channels/pairing. It is a capability:
holding it is what authorises the approval, alongside org admin.

id.description: ID is the author to approve, from the path.

shareBps.description:
ShareBps overrides this author's royalty share, in basis points (0–10000).
0 keeps the platform default. A share change never rewrites history: existing
ledger rows keep the share that was applied when they were written.

query.description: Query is the question, from the BODY. Takes precedence over `?q=`.

repo.description: Repo is the repository narrowing, from the BODY. Takes precedence over `?repo=`.

act.description: Action — the operation on the object.

sub.description: Subject — the user or role requesting access.

data.description:
Data is the flow graph — the product's nodes/edges document, verbatim:
nodes carry a piece type (webhook, schedule, http, set, branch) and its
config; edges wire them. Omit it to create an empty flow.

name.description: Name is the flow's display name.

flow.description: Flow is the id of the flow to run.

input.description:
Input is the trigger payload handed to the run, verbatim JSON object.
The run's state starts as {"trigger": input}.

data.description: Data replaces the flow graph when present, verbatim.

flow.description: Flow is the flow's id, taken from the path.

name.description: Name renames the flow when present.

before.description:
Before bounds the seed to ledger rows written before this RFC3339 instant.
Defaults to now; pass the incremental view's creation instant so the seed and
the live view never overlap and double a day.

force.description:
Force must be exactly "true" to seed a rollup that already holds rows. It is
spelled as a string, not a flag, because the guard has always compared this
value literally — "1" and "yes" do NOT force.

base_Record.description:
A collection row. `id`, `created` and `updated` are managed by Base;
all other fields are collection-defined and passed through as-is.

alreadyIncorporated.description:
AlreadyIncorporated declares an org that already has an entity, which takes
the import path (POST /v1/company/skip) instead of the formation path.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction is the state of formation: DE or WY.

name.description: Name is the proposed company name.

structure.description: Structure is the legal entity to form: c-corp, llc or dao-llc.

agentName.description: AgentName is the cloud Agent (/v1/agents) the machine will run. Required.

botVersion.description: BotVersion pins the @hanzo/bot runtime version; empty takes the default.

id.description: ID is the machine to bind, from the URL path.

name.description: Name is the bucket name to create.

bucket.description:
Bucket is the bucket's name within the org, from the path: 1–64 of
[A-Za-z0-9_], no dash.

history.description: History is how many revisions each key keeps, 1–64. 0 means 1.

maxValue.description:
MaxValue caps one value's size in bytes. 0 or less means the server's
ceiling.

ttl.description: TTL expires entries after this many SECONDS. 0 means no expiry.

data.description:
Data is the payload, carried verbatim as UTF-8 text (typically JSON).
Binary payloads belong on the NATS port.

headers.description:
Headers are optional message headers, one value per name. A Nats-Msg-Id
header is JetStream's deduplication key: a repeat within the stream's
dedup window is acknowledged as duplicate rather than stored twice.

subject.description:
Subject is the subject to publish to, in the org's own namespace — e.g.
orders.created. No wildcards.

data.description: Data is the request payload, carried verbatim as UTF-8 text.

headers.description: Headers are optional request headers, one value per name.

subject.description: Subject is the subject a responder listens on, in the org's namespace.

timeoutMs.description:
TimeoutMs bounds the wait for a reply. 0 or less means the default of
5000; anything above 30000 is clamped to 30000.

account.description: Account is the provider ad-account this campaign runs on (Meta act_<id>). Optional.

budget.description: Budget is the campaign budget in MINOR units (cents). Negative values clamp to 0.

name.description: Name is the campaign's display label. Required; trimmed and bounded to 1024 bytes.

objective.description: Objective is the campaign goal as the provider names it. Optional, bounded to 1024 bytes.

platform.description: Platform is the ad network: meta, google, tiktok or x. Empty defaults to meta.

spend.description: Spend is the amount spent so far in MINOR units (cents). Negative values clamp to 0.

status.description: Status is the lifecycle state: draft, active, paused or completed. Empty defaults to draft.

id.description: ID is the campaign to update, from the path.

audience.description: Audience is the segment or audience selector this campaign targets.

budget.description: Budget is the campaign's total budget in CENTS. Negative reads as 0.

channels.description:
Channels are the fan-out targets, at most one per kind (paid, organic,
email) and at most 12. A channel's status and provider id are server-owned:
whatever the caller sends for them is replaced with "pending".

content.description:
Content is the ordered creative set. Content[0] is the active creative and
the rest are A/B variants; at most 32, empty entries dropped.

name.description:
Name is the campaign's display name. Required; trimmed and capped at 2048
characters.

scheduleAt.description:
ScheduleAt is when the campaign should run, in unix seconds. Negative reads
as 0 (immediately).

id.description: ID is the cap to edit or remove, from the path. Unused by the list and create ops.

org.description:
Org is the tenant to act on. Required for a SuperAdmin — they must name their
target; ignored for a white-label admin, who always acts on their own org.

incorporationCountry.description:
IncorporationCountry is the ISO country the entity is incorporated in.
Optional; omitted, null or empty clears it. Any JSON scalar is accepted
and stored as its text.

name.description:
Name is the company's legal name. Required, and it must be a non-empty
string — anything else is refused with the cap table's own validation
error.

closeDate.description:
CloseDate is the date to record the round as closed on. Optional: omitted,
null or empty records TODAY. Any JSON scalar is accepted and stored as its
text, and the text is stored unparsed, so a caller that wants an ISO date
sends one.

id.description:
ID is the round to close. It is the path segment: the URL is the
addressing authority, and the org it is resolved in comes from the
caller's principal, so an id from another tenant is simply not found.

currentRelationship.description:
CurrentRelationship is how the stakeholder relates to the company, e.g.
FOUNDER, INVESTOR or EMPLOYEE. This route stores it as sent — unlike
adding a stakeholder, it is not checked against the vocabulary.

email.description:
Email is the stakeholder's email. This route stores it as sent — unlike
adding a stakeholder, it is not checked for shape or uniqueness.

id.description:
ID is the stakeholder to update. It is the path segment: the URL is the
addressing authority, and the org it is resolved in comes from the
caller's principal, so an id from another tenant is simply not found.

institutionName.description: InstitutionName names the institution, when the stakeholder is one.

name.description: Name is the stakeholder's full name.

stakeholderType.description:
StakeholderType is INDIVIDUAL or INSTITUTION. This route stores it as
sent — unlike adding a stakeholder, it is not checked against the
vocabulary.

state.description: State is the stakeholder's state or province.

streetAddress.description: StreetAddress is the stakeholder's street address.

taxId.description: TaxID is the stakeholder's tax identifier.

zipcode.description: Zipcode is the stakeholder's postal code.

account.description:
Account is the provider account this channel runs under: an ad-account, a
page, or a mailing-list id.

id.description: ID is the campaign to add the channel to, from the path.

kind.description:
Kind is the channel kind and the identity a campaign holds at most one of:
paid, organic or email.

platform.description:
Platform is the provider within the kind — meta, google, x, instagram, or
the email provider.

message.description:
Message is the founder's question for the Business AI. Required; trimmed,
and clipped to 4 KiB so a caller cannot amplify the AI prompt.

code.description:
Code is the referrer's referral code, as it appeared in their ?ref= link.
Case and surrounding whitespace do not matter.

default.description: Default marks this the org's default cluster for scheduling.

kubeconfig.description:
Kubeconfig is the cluster's kubeconfig, verbatim. Required — a body without
one is not an attach.

name.description:
Name is the fleet-local name for the cluster; lower-cased, and the key the
detach route addresses it by. Required.

provider.description:
Provider is a free-form label for where the cluster runs ("gke", "on-prem");
it is display only, not a routing key.

arr.description: ARR is annual recurring revenue in minor units (cents) of Currency.

currency.description: Currency is the ISO code ARR is denominated in; empty defaults to USD.

domainName.description: DomainName is the company's primary domain, e.g. "acme.com".

id.description:
ID names the company to update and comes from the path. A create ignores
it: the server mints the id.

idealCustomerProfile.description: ICP marks the company as an ideal-customer-profile fit.

linkedinLink.description: Linkedin is the company's LinkedIn URL.

name.description: Name is the company name. Required.

xLink.description: XLink is the company's X (Twitter) URL.

accountId.description:
AccountID is the provider account the credential should be scoped to, for the
providers whose Verify needs one (Cloudflare). Ignored by the OAuth path.

provider.description: Provider is the connector's registry id, from the :provider path segment.

token.description:
Token is the customer's provider credential. Its PRESENCE — not its value —
is what selects the apikey seal over the OAuth flow for a provider that
offers both: {"token":"…"}, even empty, is an apikey attempt (→ verify, which
answers the "token required" 400 on an empty value), while a body with no
token key (the console Connect button, `hanzo connector add` with no --token)
starts OAuth. Read on STDIN by the CLI, never argv; never logged or echoed.

githubLogin.description:
GithubLogin is the account to link. Used only when IAM holds no linked
account for the provider — a linked account is stronger proof and always wins.

login.description:
Login is the provider-neutral alias for GithubLogin, preferred when both are
sent.

provider.description: Provider is the forge to enrol with: github (the default) or gitlab.

name.description: Name is the durable consumer name: 1–64 of [A-Za-z0-9_-].

stream.description: Stream is the stream to consume, from the path.

city.description: City is where the person is based.

companyId.description: CompanyID links the contact to one of the org's companies.

email.description: Email is the person's email address.

firstName.description: FirstName is the person's given name.

id.description:
ID names the contact to update and comes from the path. A create ignores
it: the server mints the id.

jobTitle.description: JobTitle is the person's role at their company.

lastName.description: LastName is the person's family name.

linkedinLink.description: Linkedin is the person's LinkedIn URL.

phone.description: Phone is the person's phone number.

xLink.description: XLink is the person's X (Twitter) URL.

budgetTokens.description:
BudgetTokens caps the bundle's size. Clamped to [256, 32000]; 0 or absent
uses 4000.

query.description: Query is what to retrieve context for. Required, max 4000 bytes.

repo.description:
Repo narrows retrieval to one repository. Empty searches every repo the org
has indexed.

name.description:
Name is the account's label. Required, trimmed; it groups wallets and is
not itself a key.
Name is the cluster's name. Required.

region.description: Region is the provider region slug (e.g. "nyc3"). Required.

version.description: Version is the Kubernetes version slug; empty takes the provider default.

description.description: Description is a free-text label for the console. Optional, clipped to 1024 bytes.

events.description:
Events are NATS subject patterns to subscribe to (e.g. "commerce.order.>").
An empty or omitted list means EVERY event on the platform bus. Max 64
patterns, each max 256 bytes.

status.description:
Status is "active" or "disabled". Empty defaults to active. A disabled
endpoint receives no bus deliveries, but can still be exercised with
POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/test.

url.description:
URL is the https:// address each matching event is POSTed to. Required,
max 2048 bytes; http:// and every other scheme is refused, because a
webhook carries signed event data and must not travel in the clear.

displayName.description: DisplayName names the flow's initial draft version.

externalId.description: ExternalID is the caller's own id for this flow. Optional.

folderId.description: FolderID groups the flow in the builder's tree. Optional.

trigger.description:
Trigger is the root of the step tree — how the flow starts, and the action
chain that follows. Optional: a flow may be created empty and edited later.

forwarding_rules.description:
ForwardingRules are the listen→backend port mappings. Empty defaults to
plain HTTP 80→80, the same default DigitalOcean's own console applies.

name.description:
Name is the FRIENDLY name, a DNS-safe slug of at most 40 characters. The
physical DigitalOcean name is derived from it and the caller's org.

region.description: Region is the DigitalOcean region slug (nyc3, sfo3, …). Required.

size.description: Size is the DigitalOcean size slug. Empty takes DO's default.

type.description: Type is the DigitalOcean load-balancer type. Empty takes DO's default (REGIONAL).

description.description: Description is optional free text, up to 512 characters.

name.description:
Name is the queue's display handle, 1–128 printable characters. It must be
unique within the org's project. Required.

scoreConfigIds.description: ScoreConfigIDs are the eval score-configs reviewers grade against.

description.description: Description is a free-form blurb, max 4KiB.

name.description:
Name is the repo's handle, unique within the scope, and the last segment of
both clone URLs. Must match ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$; a trailing
".git" is stripped first. Required.

project.description:
Project narrows the repo to a sub-scope of the org. Omit it to use the
caller's own X-Project-Id scope; it can never widen past the caller's org.

public.description:
Public grants ANONYMOUS read (fetch) only; push and the whole control plane
stay org-authed. Defaults to false.

authHeader.description:
AuthHeader is the request header the credential is injected into, e.g.
"Authorization". Empty means the server needs no credential.

listing.description:
Listing enables a CATALOG entry instead — the id from GET /v1/tools/catalog.
The endpoint is the listing's own streamable-http remote, so a listing that
only ships a stdio package is refused: there is nothing to reach yet.

name.description:
Name labels the server for the org. Required with URL; with Listing it
defaults to the listing's own title.

secret.description:
Secret is the credential VALUE. It is sealed into KMS under a per-org ref
and never stored in SQLite, never listed, and never returned.

url.description:
URL is the server's JSON-RPC endpoint. It must be an http(s) URL naming a
PUBLIC host: loopback, link-local, private and cloud-metadata addresses are
refused here and again when the dialer connects.

ip_range.description: IPRange is the VPC's private CIDR. Empty lets DigitalOcean assign one.

name.description:
Name is the FRIENDLY name, a DNS-safe slug of at most 40 characters. The
physical DigitalOcean name is derived from it and the caller's org.

region.description: Region is the DigitalOcean region slug (nyc3, sfo3, …). Required.

id.description: ID is the flow to add a version to, from the path.

trigger.description:
Trigger is the root of the version's step tree. Optional: a version with no
trigger is created invalid, and cannot run until one is set.

accountId.description:
AccountID is the account this wallet belongs to. Required, and it must be
an account of the caller's own org — an unknown one is a 404.

agent.description:
Agent optionally narrows the wallet to one agent within the org. It becomes
a segment of the key ref, so it must be a url-safe segment with no slash.

chain.description:
Chain is the EVM chain this wallet is for, as "eip155:<n>" or a bare
decimal chain id. Optional; a Safe defaults to the Hanzo L1 (36963).

custody.description:
Custody selects the signing backend: "kms" (in-process, always available),
"mpc" or "treasury" (the deployed MPC ring), or "safe" (a Safe smart wallet
owned by an MPC key). Empty uses the deployment's default. A backend that is
not configured fails CLOSED with 503 rather than fabricating a signature.

name.description: Name is the wallet's display label. Optional.

tier.description:
Tier is the MPC wallet tier: hot, warm, cold, gas, bridge, contract_admin,
validator, quarantine or disaster_recovery. Empty defaults to hot.

accountId.description: AccountID scopes the credential where the provider's Verify needs one.

label.description: Label names this connection; empty means "default".

oauth.description:
OAuth is a bundle the CLI already obtained through its own local PKCE flow.
Present ⇒ the Adopt path; absent ⇒ the Token path.

provider.description: Provider is the user-scoped provider's registry id, from the path.

token.description:
Token is the customer-held credential for the Verify path. Read on STDIN by
the CLI, never argv; never logged, echoed, or stored outside KMS.

featured.description: Featured puts the listing on the front of the shelf, or takes it off.

hidden.description: Hidden takes the listing off the org-visible shelf, or puts it back.

id.description: ID is the listing to curate, from the path.

logo.description:
Logo is the brand mark to render, an https URL. Empty clears ours and lets
the next sync adopt the publisher's own icon again.

official.description:
Official overrides the derivation: setting it makes this answer FINAL, so
no later sync re-derives over it. That is the difference between a default
and a decision — the derivation can only tell that a domain-verified
publisher serves the endpoint, not that the product is theirs.

name.description: Name is the database name to create.

email.description: Email identifies the founder on the formation.

status.description: Status is the decision: reviewer_confirmed or failed. Nothing else is accepted.

project.description: Project is the deployed project's id. Required.

repoUrl.description:
RepoURL is the source repository the project was built from. Empty means a
hand-built project with nothing to attribute — an honest no-op, not an error.

label.description:
Label names this connection so one user can hold several per provider
("work", "personal"). Empty means "default". 1-64 of [A-Za-z0-9._-].

provider.description: Provider is the user-scoped provider's registry id, from the path.

content.description:
Record content varies by type:
- A: IPv4 address (e.g. 1.2.3.4)
- AAAA: IPv6 address
- CNAME: Target hostname
- MX: Mail server hostname
- TXT: Text value (auto-quoted)
- SRV: weight port target (priority set separately)
- NS: Nameserver hostname
- CAA: flags tag value (e.g. 0 issue letsencrypt.org)

priority.description: Required for MX and SRV records

name.description: Name is the custom domain to attach, e.g. "www.acme.com".

project.description: Project is the Pages project name, from the path.

id.description: ID is the item within that namespace.

kind.description: Kind is the item's namespace: "model", "provider" or "feature".

connector.description: Connector names the stored credential to reach this endpoint with.

locator.description:
Locator addresses the resource. For a git source it is the https clone URL on
the provider's own host, with no embedded credentials; for a native target it
is the repository name.

provider.description:
Provider is the platform: github or gitlab for a source; a target defaults to
the native Hanzo Git plane.

signed.description:
Signed, when present, overrides what the provider reports — the manual path
for a provider whose webhook is not wired. Omit it to take the provider's answer.

rubric.description: Custom rubric (when not a pre-built metric)

backend.description: Evaluation backend — native Hanzo engine or DigitalOcean GenAI

preset.description: Named preset to reuse a saved configuration

distinct_id.description: DistinctID is the identity the flags are evaluated for. Required.

groups.description: Groups are the group-level properties, keyed by group type index.

person_properties.description: PersonProperties are the person-level properties conditions match against.

batch.description:
Batch is the most messages to return. 0 or less means 1; anything above
100 is clamped to 100.

name.description: Name is the consumer, from the path.

stream.description: Stream is the stream, from the path.

waitMs.description:
WaitMs is how long to wait for the batch to fill before answering with
what arrived. 0 or less means the default of 5000; clamped to 30000.

content.description:
Content is the file's full text. Max 1 MiB per file; binary files should
simply be omitted rather than sent.

path.description: Path is the file's repo-relative path, e.g. "internal/store/db.go".

documentIds.description:
DocumentIDs are the documents to file. At least one is required, and every
one must belong to the caller's org — a filing can never reach across orgs.

jurisdiction.description: Jurisdiction is the state or agency the filing is for, e.g. "DE".

data.description:
Data is the workflow graph (the product's nodes/edges document),
verbatim. Omit it to create an empty workflow.

description.description: Description says what the workflow does.

name.description:
Name is the workflow's display name, unique within the org's project
(the product de-duplicates by suffixing).

input.description: Input is the run's chat input value, handed to the graph's input node.

session.description:
Session groups runs into one conversation; the product mints one when
absent and returns it in the response.

tweaks.description:
Tweaks override component fields for this run only (the product's
tweaks document), verbatim.

workflow.description: Workflow is the UUID of the workflow to run.

data.description: Data replaces the workflow graph when present, verbatim.

description.description: Description replaces the description when present.

locked.description: Locked freezes or unfreezes the workflow against edits when present.

name.description: Name renames the workflow when present.

workflow.description: Workflow is the workflow's UUID, taken from the path.

founders.description:
Founders is every founding stakeholder. Each needs a name and an email, and
equityBps between 0 and 10000 (1% == 100 bps).

framework_Document.description:
A schemaless document. Field data is carried at the top level alongside the
envelope keys (name/doctype/docstatus/createdAt/updatedAt). Password fields
are redacted in responses. On write, only the field data is read.

entry_port.description: EntryPort is the port the load balancer listens on.

entry_protocol.description: EntryProtocol is the protocol the load balancer listens with (http, https, tcp).

target_port.description: TargetPort is the backend port traffic is forwarded to.

target_protocol.description: TargetProtocol is the protocol used to reach the backend droplets.

data.description:
Data supplies every merge field the template declares, keyed by field key.
Every declared field is REQUIRED: a missing one is refused with 400 rather
than rendered as a blank into a contract.

templateId.description:
TemplateID is the template to render. Required; resolved for the caller's
org, so an override wins over the built-in.

state.description:
State is the GitHub issue state to walk: "open" (the default), "closed" or
"all". Anything else is a 400.

all.description:
All imports every repository the installation grants, instead of naming
them. Archived and disabled repositories are skipped either way — they
cannot be fetched.

repos.description:
Repos names the repositories to import, either owner-qualified
("hanzo-apps/ai") or as a bare name ("ai"); a trailing ".git" is stripped.
A bare name that matches more than one granted repository is an error
rather than a guess, because one Hanzo org may hold several GitHub
installations and a name is only unique within an owner.
Ignored when all is true.

branch.description:
Branch is the legacy source branch; empty defaults to the repo's own default
branch. Ignored when buildType is "workflow".

buildType.description:
BuildType selects the builder: "workflow" builds via GitHub Actions, anything
else builds from the branch source above.

path.description:
Path is the source directory within the branch: "/" (the default) or "/docs".
GitHub allows no others.

repo.description: Repo is the repository, from the :repo path segment.

branch.description: Branch switches the legacy source branch. Empty leaves the source alone.

buildType.description: BuildType switches the builder: "legacy" or "workflow". Empty leaves it.

cname.description:
CNAME is the custom domain. Omit to leave it alone, "" to clear it, or a
valid FQDN to set it.

httpsEnforced.description: HTTPSEnforced toggles GitHub's enforce-HTTPS bit. Omit to leave it alone.

path.description:
Path is the source directory to pair with Branch: "/" (the default) or
"/docs". Read only when Branch is given.

repo.description: Repo is the repository, from the :repo path segment.

description.description:
Description is the customer's message. Optional; it becomes the ticket's
description AND the opening entry of its conversation thread. Clipped at
16 KiB.

email.description:
Email is how the support team replies. Required; clipped at 320 characters
(the RFC 5321 maximum). It is recorded as the ticket's customer, and it is
not verified.

priority.description:
Priority is Low, Medium, High or Urgent, case-insensitively. Anything else —
including omitting it — is recorded as Medium rather than refused.

subject.description:
Subject is the one-line summary of the problem. Required; longer than 300
characters is clipped rather than refused.

iam_controllers.CheckPasswordRequest.description: Credentials to verify. Handler binds object.User; only these fields are consumed.

iam_controllers.LinkForm.description: Unlink a federated provider from a user (controllers.LinkForm).

username.description: Email, phone, or username; must resolve to a user

range.description: Range is an optional A1 range within the sheet; empty reads the default range.

spreadsheetId.description: SpreadsheetID is a Google Sheets id. Required.

folderId.description: FolderID is a Google Drive folder id. Required.

files.description:
Files is the full set of files to index. Required and non-empty; max 20000
files, 1 MiB per file and 1 GiB in total. Unchanged files are skipped by
content hash, so re-sending the whole tree is cheap.

prune.description:
Prune deletes indexed files that are NOT in this request — which makes the
call a full sync of the repo rather than an upsert. Only pass it when Files
is the complete tree.

repo.description:
Repo is the repository label to index under. Required, max 200 bytes. It is
a stored column value, not a filesystem path.

tool.description:
Tool is the registry name of the capability to activate (or deactivate) for
the caller's own org and project. Required.

assignee.description: Assignee is who owns the issue, at most 256 characters. Empty unassigns it.

description.description: Description is the issue body, at most 32768 characters.

key.description: Key is the issue's project, from the path.

num.description: Num is the issue's number within that project, from the path.

priority.description: Priority is none, urgent, high, medium or low. Empty resets it to none.

status.description:
Status moves the issue between board columns: backlog, todo, in_progress,
done or canceled. Empty resets it to backlog.

title.description: Title is the issue's one-line summary. Non-empty, at most 512 characters.

assignee.description: Assignee is the reviewer this item is for, up to 512 characters.

objectId.description: ObjectID is the referenced object's id, paired with objectType.

objectType.description:
ObjectType is TRACE, OBSERVATION or SESSION — the generic form, paired
with objectId.

observationId.description:
ObservationID references an observation — the console-friendly form of
objectType=OBSERVATION.

sessionId.description:
SessionID references a session — the console-friendly form of
objectType=SESSION.

traceId.description:
TraceID references a trace — the console-friendly form of
objectType=TRACE.

id.description: ID is the job (activity) id, from the URL path.

reason.description: Reason is recorded on the cancellation; empty records "canceled from console".

run.description:
Run is the run id; empty defaults to the job id, which is what the dispatcher
sets (runId == activityId == prompt_id), so the common case sends no body.

type.description:
Type is the key class to act on: "secret" (sk-, session-equivalent, belongs
on a server) or "publishable" (pk-, org-identifying, safe in a browser
bundle). Omitted means secret, which is what every existing caller means.

bucket.description: Bucket is the bucket, from the path.

key.description: Key is the key, from the path.

value.description: Value is the value, carried verbatim as UTF-8 text (typically JSON).

stream.description: Stream is the stream name, from the path.

name.description:
Name is the local repo to mirror into, from the :name path segment. It is
CREATED on first use.

project.description:
Project is the sub-scope to land the repo in; empty uses the caller's own,
exactly as a create would.

source.description:
Source is the http(s) git URL to fetch from. The host is SSRF-guarded and
the shared mirror credential is only sent to allowlisted hosts.

host.description:
Host is an optional assertion of the target's hostname. The authoritative
host is the one in URL; a value that disagrees with it is refused.

name.description:
Name is the repo whose advanced refs are pushed downstream, from the :name
path segment.

url.description:
URL is the downstream https git remote. Must be https to an allowlisted
host (github.com / gitlab.com); any embedded credentials are stripped.
Required.

add.description:
Add is the product ids to turn ON. Each must already be an ACTIVE entitlement
of the org's plan, unless the caller is a platform super admin.

remove.description: Remove is the product ids to turn OFF. Disabling is never gated.

title.description: Title is the namespace's display title. Cloudflare mints the id.

batch.description: Batch is how many messages to pull (1–1000, default 1).

expires.description: Expires is how long to wait for messages, e.g. "5s" (default "30s", max "60s").

name.description: Name is the consumer name, from the path.

no_wait.description: NoWait answers immediately with whatever is available instead of waiting.

stream.description: Stream is the stream name, from the path.

notify_Channel.description:
Delivery channel. Only `sms` and `email` are supported by the cloud
fold; `voice` and `whatsapp` are defined by the notify types but not
wired here.

notify_SendRequest.description:
Notification send request (`notify/pkg/types.SendRequest`). Delivery
content is either a raw `subject`/`body`, or a template resolved from
`template_id`/`event` rendered against `template_vars`.

body.description:
Raw message body. When non-empty it wins verbatim and no template is
rendered.

event.description:
Event-catalog identifier. Also used as a fallback template id when
`template_id` is unset (the IAM OTP path sends `event: iam.otp_sent`
with no `template_id`).

idempotency_key.description:
Per-tenant deduplication key. Accepted on the wire; the sync fold
does not persist a Message row.

provider.description:
Pins a specific provider service name (e.g. `twilio`, `plivo`,
`twilio_email`, `mail`). When omitted the fold picks the org's
default for the channel from configured KMS credentials.

send_at.description:
RFC3339 schedule time for async dispatch. Async is not available in
the fold, so a set value has no effect on the sync path.

subject.description: Raw subject; used verbatim when `body` is set (no-template path).

template_id.description:
Built-in template identifier. When `body` is empty, the template is
resolved from `template_id` or, failing that, `event`.

template_vars.description:
Free-form variables the template is rendered against (e.g. `otp`,
`app`, `recipient`). A missing `app` defaults to `Hanzo`.

to.description:
Destination address(es). Phone number for SMS, email for email.
Multiple recipients fan out into one provider call each and produce
one response entry per recipient.

o11y_BuilderQuery.description: Composite builder-query payload. The console-shaped composite (start, end, step, compositeQuery with queryType and builderQueries) is passed through to the internal query engine unchanged; the org is pinned server-side and the client never supplies a raw PromQL/SQL fragment.

o11y_IngestEvent.description: One LLM-observability event — a typed envelope whose body is the type-specific payload.

account.description: Account is the account label the flow reported; sanitized on ingest.

refresh.description: Refresh is the refresh token. It is sealed and NEVER handed back out.

name.description:
Name is the organization's display name. Ignored when personal is true, which
derives the name from the caller's own username instead.

personal.description:
Personal asks for the caller's own workspace: the name is derived from their
username and the slug auto-suffixes to stay unique. Meaningless — and refused
— for a caller who already has an organization.

amount.description: Amount is the deal value in minor units (cents) of Currency.

closeDate.description: CloseDate is the expected close, as a unix second (0 = unset).

companyId.description: CompanyID links the deal to one of the org's companies.

currency.description: Currency is the ISO code Amount is denominated in; empty defaults to USD.

id.description:
ID names the opportunity to update and comes from the path. A create
ignores it: the server mints the id.

name.description: Name is the deal name. Required.

pointOfContactId.description: PointOfContact links the deal to one of the org's contacts.

stage.description:
Stage is the pipeline stage: NEW, SCREENING, MEETING, PROPOSAL or CUSTOMER
(case-insensitive). Empty defaults to NEW.

display.description:
Display is the name shown for the org on that board: 1-40 characters of
letters, digits, space, dot, underscore, apostrophe or hyphen. Left empty on a
listing opt-in it defaults to the org id.

listed.description:
Listed publishes the org on the cross-org global board when true, and withdraws
it when false.

id.description: ID is the application to move, from the path.

note.description:
Note is a free-text comment recorded on the timeline, with or without a
stage change.

reason.description: Reason records WHY, and is required to reject.

stage.description:
Stage is the stage to move to: applied, screened, qualified,
credits-offered, onboarded or rejected. Omit to leave the stage alone.

externalId.description: ExternalID sets the caller's own id for this flow.

folderId.description: FolderID moves the flow in the builder's tree.

id.description: ID is the flow to update, from the path.

metadata.description: Metadata replaces the caller's opaque JSON.

publishedVersionId.description:
PublishedVersionID pins the version runs execute. It must name a version OF
THIS FLOW; empty clears the pin, so runs take the latest version again.

name.description: Name is the repo to update, from the :name path segment.

public.description:
Public flips anonymous read access. Omit it and the request is refused —
there is nothing else to update yet.

id.description: ID is the session to update, from the path.

project.description:
Project tags the product this session built; Published is the author's
decision to let anyone read the story (provenance.go). Both are pointers so
"absent" and "cleared" are different requests.

target.description: Target re-dispatches a session to a run-target (the #48 association). "" detaches.

terminal.description:
Terminal publishes (or, with "", withdraws) the URL this session's live
terminal can be watched at. A pointer so "absent" and "withdrawn" are
different requests: a session that stops sharing must be able to say so.

actor.description:
Actor is the loop-guard identity the sync writes as. Omitted, the stored actor
stands.

direction.description: Direction is both, pull, push or off. Omitted, the stored direction stands.

id.description: ID is the sync to update, from the path.

trigger.description: Trigger is webhook, poll or manual. Omitted, the stored trigger stands.

id.description: ID is the target to update, from the path.

metrics.description: present => a heartbeat; the server stamps its time

amountCents.description:
AmountCents is how much to pay, in cents. Must be positive and can never
exceed the author's pending royalty (accrued minus paid).

id.description: ID is the author to pay, from the path.

method.description:
Method is how it settles: "credits" issues a grant into the author's wallet;
wire, paypal and the like are record-only. Required.

reference.description:
Reference is the operator's external reference for a cash settlement — a wire
confirmation, a PayPal transaction id.

feeds.description:
Feeds is the RSS/Atom feed URLs to read, at most 64. Each must be an
http(s) URL whose host is on the server's allowlist — the SSRF guard is
applied here, at the write, so a stored pipeline can never name a host the
fetcher would refuse. Blank entries are dropped and duplicates collapse.

filters.description:
Filters narrows the merged feed. Terms are trimmed, de-duplicated
case-insensitively, and capped at 64 per axis.

revenueShareBps.description:
RevenueShareBps is the share of net platform revenue a sweep accrues into the
reserve fund, in basis points. 0–10000; 2000 (20%) is the platform default.

autoScale.description: AutoScale turns the provider's cluster autoscaler on for this pool.

clusterId.description: ClusterID is the cluster to add the pool to, from the URL path.

count.description: Count is how many nodes the pool starts with.

minNodes.description:
MinNodes and MaxNodes bound the autoscaler; they are ignored unless
AutoScale is set.

name.description: Name is the pool's name.

provider.description:
Provider is the cloud the cluster lives on (e.g. "digitalocean"). Required —
Visor routes the create by it. Accepted from the body or ?provider=.

size.description: Size is the provider size slug for each node (e.g. "s-4vcpu-8gb").

clusterId.description: ClusterID and PoolID address the pool, from the URL path.

count.description:
Count is the node count to scale TO — an absolute target, not a delta, and
never negative.

provider.description: Provider is the cloud the cluster lives on. Required; body or ?provider=.

description.description: Description is the board's free-form blurb, at most 32768 characters.

key.description: Key is the project to update, from the path.

name.description: Name is the project's display name. Non-empty, at most 256 characters.

id.description: ID is the queued deployment to complete, from the path.

keys.description:
Keys is the manifest CI just uploaded, RELATIVE to the deployment prefix. It
is what replaces `aws s3 sync --delete`: an upload grant authorizes writes
only, so CI cannot remove a file, and cloud reconciles the prefix against
this list instead (grant.go). Omit it and nothing is deleted — the prefix
only grows, which is the old pre-grant behaviour and a safe default.

slug.description: Slug is the project the deployment belongs to, from the path.

analytics.description:
Analytics is the opt-OUT for the wired-by-default analytics beacon: absent
(nil) ⇒ ON (the default); explicit false ⇒ off. A pointer so "unset" is
distinguishable from "false" — the only way to turn the default off.

upstream.description:
Upstream/License credit the third-party work this project was published
from. Taken from any caller: disclaiming authorship can only cost the
publisher credit, so it needs no gate (see Project.Upstream).

visibility.description:
Visibility is "public" (the default when absent) or "private". Publishing
publicly is ungated — that is the point of a community. Going PRIVATE is
the paid feature, so an unfunded org asking for it is refused rather than
silently downgraded (see resolve).

domains.description:
Domains are the custom hostnames to attach, in order. An empty list is a
400 rather than a clear — releasing a host is its own call.

slug.description: Slug is the site the hosts attach to, from the path.

name.description: target project name (optional; defaults to the parent's title)

slug.description: parent slug to fork — catalog template or published project (required)

target.description:
Target overrides the derived project slug (optional; defaults to the
parent slug). Kept distinct from Slug so callers can rename on fork.

variant.description:
Variant picks a template's format/page/theme (optional; defaults to the
template's first shape). This is the axis the catalog used to spend
sibling slugs on, so it is expressed here, where the user's preference is.

slug.description: Slug is the site to publish, from the path.

source.description:
Source is the build output to promote, as a path RELATIVE to your org's own
storage space — never a URL and never a bucket. The org segment is prepended
server-side from the validated principal, so the worst a hostile source can
address is something your own org already owns.

hidden.description:
Hidden is MODERATION, and the only admin-gated field on this body: it pulls
a public project out of the catalogue from admin.hanzo.ai without editing
the publisher's own visibility choice, so un-hiding restores exactly what
they asked for. A tenant sending it is ignored.

slug.description:
Slug is the project to update, from the path. The URL is the addressing
authority — a `slug` in the body cannot move the write to another project.

upstream.description:
Upstream/License credit the third-party work this app was published from —
settable after the fact, because the demos that need crediting most are the
ones already live. Pointers so "" clears a credit and absent leaves it.

visibility.description:
Visibility flips an existing project between "public" and "private". Same
ONE rule as at create: public is free, private needs a paid plan.

projects_GitDeployRequest.description: Body for the git deploy mode (Content-Type application/json).

source.description: Deploy source selector; "git" for the CI build path.

active.description: Active is the master switch: false parks the offer without deleting it.

end.description: End is when the offer closes (RFC3339).

plans.description: Plans are the plan ids the offer applies to.

start.description: Start is when the offer opens (RFC3339).

labels.description: Labels is free-form taxonomy, each up to 64 characters, capped at 32 entries.

name.description:
Name is the org-unique handle AND the URL segment the prompt is addressed by:
1-64 characters matching ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$. "metrics", "new" and
"catalog" are reserved. A name that already exists appends a new version.

prompt.description:
Prompt is the template body, capped at 64 KiB. It holds template text only —
never a secret.

tags.description: Tags is free-form taxonomy under the same bounds as Labels.

type.description: Type labels the template's kind; defaults to "text".

name.description: Name is the provider the overlay belongs to, from the URL.

category.description: Category groups the kit in the gallery browser.

demo.description: Demo is the deployed site itself, when there is one.

description.description: Description is the browse-card blurb, max 4096 characters.

features.description: Features are the highlights the card lists, at most 32.

framework.description: Framework is the stack the kit is built on ("Next.js 14").

preview.description: Preview is the still image the browse card renders, max 4096 characters.

slug.description: Slug is the kit's identity — lowercase alphanumeric with dashes, max 40.

source.description: Source is the repository the kit is forked from, max 4096 characters.

title.description: Title is the display name. Required, max 200 characters.

useCase.description: UseCase is what the kit is for, in a phrase.

variants.description: Variants are the shapes this kit ships in, at most 32; the fork picks one.

category.description: Category groups the listing in the shop window.

description.description: Description is the long copy, clipped at 4096 characters.

price.description:
Price is the per-call price as a decimal USD string, exact to 18 places —
"0.0025" is a quarter of a cent and stays one. Empty or "0" (the default)
publishes it free; any positive price makes the listing monetized and
requires Recipient.

public.description: Public makes the listing discoverable by other orgs. Private otherwise.

recipient.description:
Recipient is the seller's payout wallet ID, in the publishing org — the
wallet x402 pays. Required for a monetized listing.

title.description: Title is the shop-window name, 1-200 characters. Required.

tool.description:
Tool is the registry name of the capability being offered. It must already
resolve in the publisher's own scope — there are no phantom listings.

files.description: Files purges exactly the listed URLs — at most 30, Cloudflare's per-request cap.

purge_everything.description: Everything drops the zone's entire edge cache.

zone.description: Zone is the 32-hex Cloudflare zone id, from the path.

content.description: Content is the file's bytes, carried per Encoding.

path.description: Path is repo-relative. Absolute or traversing paths are refused.

branch.description:
Branch to advance; empty means "main". A fresh branch that is the repo's
first also becomes HEAD.

files.description:
Files are added to or overwritten on the branch tip — files already there
and not listed SURVIVE. At least one, at most 5000, 32 MiB each.

message.description: Message is the commit message; empty gets a generated one.

name.description:
Name is the repo to push into, from the :name path segment. It is CREATED
on first push if it does not exist.

publicKey.description:
PublicKey is one OpenSSH authorized-key line ("ssh-ed25519 AAAA… you@host").
Required; a line that does not parse is refused and never stored.

title.description:
Title labels the key in the console. Max 256 chars; when omitted the
comment on the key line is used.

host.description: Execution context — where this session runs (all optional).

project.description:
The readable build (provenance.go): which product this session builds, and
whether its story may be read by the world.

provider.description: Account tag — the linked AI account this session ran under (login manager).

terminal.description:
Terminal is the URL this session's live terminal is published at, so the
console can watch it. Optional — a session that publishes nothing is still
a session.

image.description: Image is the repository name inside the org's namespace (e.g. "cloud").

category.description: Category groups the kit in the gallery browser.

demo.description: Demo is the deployed site itself, when there is one.

features.description: Features are the highlights the card lists, at most 32.

source.description: Source is the repository the kit is forked from, max 4096 characters.

title.description: Title is the display name. Required, max 200 characters.

useCase.description: UseCase is what the kit is for, in a phrase.

variants.description: Variants are the shapes this kit ships in, at most 32; the fork picks one.

account.description: Account is the linked account the window was metered from.

cachedInputTokens.description: CachedInputTokens is the prompt tokens the provider served from cache.

confidence.description: Confidence says how much the counters below mean.

costCents.description: CostCents is what the window cost on the PROVIDER's own plan, in US cents.

costLimitCents.description: CostLimitCents is the plan's spend ceiling for the window, in US cents.

currency.description: Currency is the provider's currency when it is not US cents.

inputTokens.description: InputTokens is prompt tokens consumed in the window.

kind.description:
Kind is subscription or apikey. Empty is accepted; anything else is
refused.

lane.description: Lane is the meter lane within the account.

machine.description: Machine is the host whose meter read the window. Required on every sample.

outputTokens.description: OutputTokens is completion tokens produced in the window.

plan.description: Plan is the provider plan the account is on, e.g. a Claude Max plan.

provider.description:
Provider is the upstream the account belongs to, e.g. anthropic. Required
on every sample.

requests.description: Requests is how many requests the window covers.

resetsAt.description: ResetsAt is when the measured window rolls over, RFC3339.

samples.description:
Samples is the batch form: every lane a poller measured, in one call. When
it is non-empty the top-level sample fields are ignored.

synthetic.description: Synthetic marks a window the meter inferred rather than read.

totalTokens.description: TotalTokens is the window's total tokens.

usedPct.description: UsedPct is how much of the window's allowance is consumed, 0–100.

window.description:
Window is the window class: 6h, day, week or month. Required, and a class
this surface does not know is refused rather than rewritten.

windowMinutes.description:
WindowMinutes is the window's real length in minutes, as the meter reports
it.

windowStart.description:
WindowStart is when the measured window opened, RFC3339. This is how a
backfill states WHICH window it measured; the server always owns the
observation clock, so there is no timestamp field.

branch.description:
Branch, CommitSha and Diffstat describe what the run produced; Error is the
failure when OK is false. Each is clamped, never rejected.

id.description: ID is the machine reporting, from the path.

ok.description: OK is whether the run succeeded; Changed whether it produced any commit.

runId.description: RunID is the routed run being completed, from the path.

pattern.description: Pattern is the URL pattern to bind, e.g. "acme.com/api/*".

script.description:
Script is the Worker script to dispatch to. Omit it to leave the pattern
bound to no script, which is how Cloudflare expresses "bypass the Worker here".

zone.description: Zone is the 32-hex Cloudflare zone id, from the path.

action.description: Action is the name of the connector action to invoke.

auth.description:
Auth is the caller's resolved credential for the connector, handed to the
action verbatim. Its shape is whatever the connector's auth descriptor
declares (a token string, an object), so it is opaque here.

id.description: ID is the connector to run, from the path.

props.description: Props are the action's input properties, keyed by property name.

documentIds.description: DocumentIDs are data room document ids to raise a signature request over. Required.

signers.description: Signers are the recipients, each a name and an email. Required.

chainId.description:
ChainID is the EVM chain the Safe transaction is bound to. 0 uses the
wallet's own chain, or the Hanzo L1 (36963) when it is chain-agnostic.

data.description: Data is the call data, hex-encoded.

nonce.description: Nonce is the Safe's transaction nonce.

to.description: To is the transaction's target address.

value.description: Value is the native-token amount to send, as a decimal string in wei.

gpuUtil.description:
GPUUtil is accelerator utilization as a fraction 0..1; the warehouse clamps
anything outside that.

gpus.description:
GPUs is how many accelerators the reading covers, GPUModel the representative
model name.

host.description: Host is the node's hostname, for display.

memUsed.description: MemUsed and MemFree are host memory in bytes.

unit.description:
Unit is the reporting node's own id — the same id it registered under, and
the key the board joins this series onto. Required.

account.description: Account is the linked account the window was metered from.

cachedInputTokens.description: CachedInputTokens is the prompt tokens the provider served from cache.

costLimitCents.description: CostLimitCents is the plan's spend ceiling for the window, in US cents.
